## Eight South American countries in 32 days: what to expect from this extensive itinerary

[A journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/) is ideal for travellers who want to experience cities, the ocean, waterfalls, the Andes, salt flats, ancient monuments and island wildlife on a single holiday. The Ada Tours itinerary takes in [Brazil](/brazil/), [Argentina](/argentina/), [Uruguay](/uruguay/), [Chile](/chile/), [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Peru](/peru/), [Ecuador](/ecuador/) and [Colombia](/colombia/). It covers 32 days and 31 nights, with frequent journeys, hotel changes and different arrangements for individual excursions.

Below is the itinerary in day-by-day sequence. When choosing this tour, it is worth considering the pace, altitude in the Andes, combination of group and private excursions, included transport and connecting flights. The length of the trip makes it possible to visit many regions, but leaves relatively few free days.

## Geography and itinerary sequence

| Itinerary stage | Main experiences |
|---|---|
| Brazil and Argentina | Rio, both sides of Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires |
| Uruguay and Chile | Montevideo, Santiago, the Atacama |
| Bolivia and Peru | Uyuni, Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu |
| Ecuador and Colombia | Galapagos Islands, Medellin, Cartagena, Bogota |

### From Rio and Iguazu to Montevideo

After arriving in São Paulo, the main city sightseeing programme begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Corcovado and its Christ the Redeemer statue, Sugarloaf Mountain and the historic centre reveal different sides of the city. The waterfalls come next: [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) in Brazil and [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) in Argentina. Panoramic viewpoints from the Brazilian bank and walking trails on the Argentine side complement one another; crossing the border is a separate stage of the itinerary.

After Iguazu, the plan includes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a city tour and an evening of tango with dinner. [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited **on a day trip from Buenos Aires**. This is a substantial stop in Uruguay, but not a multi-day tour of the country.

### The Atacama, Bolivian lagoons and Uyuni: a demanding section

The journey continues via [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), then on to Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). This section involves jeep travel, changing road surfaces, potentially cold nights and considerable elevation.

Altitude sickness is possible in the highlands, and a stop in San Pedro de Atacama helps travellers prepare for the higher elevations ahead. Good physical fitness alone does not eliminate altitude-related risks. It is sensible to avoid excessive exertion during the first days and discuss any individual restrictions with a doctor in advance, especially if you have a heart or respiratory condition. After Bolivia, the route continues through [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and Tiwanaku to Lake Titicaca.

### Peru: trains, archaeology and high-altitude travel

The Peruvian section starts in [Puno and at Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). A tourist coach then takes travellers to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), stopping along the way. The next major destination is [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). A visit requires coordination of the train service, entry time, permitted route through the site and return journey. Train tickets and admission tickets are included in the agreed programme.

After Cusco comes [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) and its own city excursion. If Inca archaeological sites interest you most, and the full eight-country route feels too intensive, compare this journey with [tours focused on Peru](/peru/tour/).

### Galapagos: a choice between two excursion itineraries

The Ecuador section includes Quito, the equator line and the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). One day offers **two alternative routes**: North Seymour and Bachas **or** South Plaza and Cape Carrión. One of these alternatives is included, with the specific option confirmed after booking. The programme does not promise visits to all four places.

This distinction also matters for conservation: Galapagos visits depend on designated routes, national park rules and sea conditions. Sightings of particular animals cannot be guaranteed in advance.

### The Colombian finale

In Colombia, the journey takes in [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/) and Guatapé, followed by [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/), with an excursion to the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá. The final day includes a flight from Bogota to São Paulo and a connection to the international flight home. Return tickets need to fit this transport sequence, rather than merely the date on which the sightseeing portion ends in Bogota.

## Included services and important distinctions

The programme includes accommodation in **4-star hotels**, domestic flights, all itinerary transfers with a driver, the specified excursions and admission tickets, the train to Machu Picchu and explicitly listed meals. The format is mixed: some visits are conducted in groups, others privately.

Russian-speaking guides accompany excursions in Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago, La Paz, Cusco, Lima, Quito, Medellin, Cartagena and Bogota. English-speaking guides accompany trips to Montevideo, Uyuni, Titicaca, Machu Picchu, the Galapagos, Guatapé and Zipaquirá. **A single Russian-speaking guide throughout all 32 days cannot be guaranteed.**

International flights, optional excursions, meals and drinks not listed in the programme, tips and personal expenses are charged separately. At Iguazu, optional activities include the Bird Park and Macuco Safari; in Chile, the Maipo Valley wineries and an evening astronomy excursion in the Atacama are optional. Availability of the latter also depends on the lunar calendar. Rates differ for a place in a shared double room and single occupancy; the final quote is confirmed at booking, taking the flights into account.

## Preparing for the trip

Over the course of a month, travellers move from light clothing for the hot coast to warm layers for the highlands and back to tropical conditions. Comfortable footwear, sun protection, clothing for cool nights, preparation for several flights and enough time to pack on early-departure days will all be useful.

Visa, transit and health requirements depend on nationality, specific connecting routes and travel dates. There is no single entry permit covering all eight countries. Before booking, check the entry rules for every participant and the requirements for visiting the Galapagos. To compare less intensive itineraries, see our [multi-country tours catalogue](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about the eight-country journey

### Is this a relaxing holiday or an intensive trip?

It is intensive. The programme includes numerous flights, early departures, drives on mountain roads and transitions between climate zones. Travellers need to be comfortable spending long periods on the road.

### Are all excursions conducted in Russian?

No. The language of the guide varies by country and by the programme for each day. Both Russian-speaking and English-speaking guides are involved.

### Can we visit both Galapagos alternatives?

One of the two routes is included in the price. The specific choice is confirmed after booking.

### Do we need to prepare for altitude in Bolivia and Peru?

Yes. Elevation and the rate of ascent affect wellbeing regardless of overall fitness. The route includes an acclimatisation stage; individual risks should be discussed with a doctor.

### Are international flights included?

No. International flights are paid for separately; domestic flights specified in the programme are included.

## A 33-day grand VIP tour of South America: how the journey works

Our private itinerary combines **Peru, Bolivia and Chile** over **33 days and 32 nights**. What sets it apart from a conventional three-country journey is the nature of its individual stages: an Amazon cruise aboard **Aqua Nera**, the **Hiram Bingham** train to Machu Picchu and the **Belmond Andean Explorer** from Cusco towards Lake Titicaca. Bolivia's salt flat, the Atacama Desert, Easter Island and two regions of southern Chile follow.

This format is designed for travellers who appreciate South American archaeology and nature, as well as the cruise, exceptional train journeys and sightseeing flights as experiences in their own right. Nearly every new stage brings a change in transport and climate. It is therefore important to consider **not only the list of attractions but also flight frequency, recovery time and the arrangements for each service**.

## Four sections of the itinerary and their highlights

| Stage | Highlights |
|---|---|
| Days 1–8 | Lima, Nazca, Ballestas Islands, Aqua Nera cruise |
| Days 9–17 | Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu, Titicaca, Uyuni |
| Days 18–24 | Atacama, Santiago, Easter Island |
| Days 25–33 | Patagonia, Lake District, Marble Caves |

**Peru** begins in the historic neighbourhoods of [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) and with an air-and-sea excursion to Nazca and the Ballestas Islands. Days 4–8 feature a **five-day, four-night Aqua Nera cruise** departing from the Iquitos area. Here the style of travel changes altogether: rather than travelling overland, guests watch the rainforest from the river and join excursions organised by the ship. The sequence of river outings depends on the cruise's actual itinerary.

After the Amazon, the route returns via Lima to the Peruvian Andes. The [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) includes Moray, Maras, Pisac and Ollantaytambo. The Hiram Bingham train takes travellers to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), followed by another exceptional experience: a helicopter excursion to Vinicunca. UNESCO recognises the Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu as a site of both cultural and natural heritage. The separate admission ticket, permitted visiting route and aviation arrangements are coordinated for the chosen date.

From Cusco, the Belmond Andean Explorer heads towards [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The itinerary includes a night aboard the train and visits to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) and [Taquile](/peru/place/taquile-island/). Travellers then cross into Bolivia, visit Tiwanaku and arrive in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/).

**The Bolivian section** centres on the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) and high-altitude lagoons on the way to Chile. Accommodation on the salt flat is planned at Palacio de Sal. The salt surface changes with the weather and season: during wet periods it may reflect the sky, while in dry conditions a vast white crust becomes visible. The actual effect and accessible areas depend on water levels.

The journey continues to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile. The programme here includes the El Tatio geysers, Moon Valley and a telescope-based astronomy excursion. After Santiago comes a flight to [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), with visits to the Rano Kau crater, Orongo, ahu ceremonial platforms and moai, including Ahu Tongariki. Rapa Nui National Park protects much of the island's cultural heritage. This is a separate flight, not a short excursion from Santiago.

## Patagonia and the Lake District: the final stages

From day 25, the itinerary moves south through Chile. A stay at **The Singular Patagonia** is planned in Puerto Natales, followed by a day in Torres del Paine National Park. Mountain walks and sightseeing stops depend directly on the weather, so their actual order may differ from the preliminary plan.

After a flight to Puerto Montt, travellers continue to Puerto Varas, Lake Llanquihue and Osorno Volcano. Petrohué, Chiloé Island and Ancud follow. The visit to the penguin colony at Puñihuil is weather-dependent.

The final nature-focused stage runs through Balmaceda and the Carretera Austral area to the [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/) on General Carrera Lake. The journey ends with a return to Santiago and departure. Patagonia and the Lake District differ from the Atacama in rainfall, temperatures and road conditions, so luggage and clothing must suit several climate zones.

## What the private format offers and what needs to be agreed

We offer the route as a **private journey**, including special aviation and rail experiences. These include a private aircraft flight over Nazca, a yacht trip to the Ballestas Islands and helicopter flights to Vinicunca and the VIK winery. Such experiences genuinely distinguish it from the [general catalogue of multi-country journeys](/multi-country/).

However, **a fixed price, departure dates and the final comprehensive list of included expenses have not yet been established**. These are agreed when the personal proposal is prepared. It should not be assumed that every mentioned flight, restaurant, hotel or private escort service is included within one published price.

Before confirming the journey, it is useful to review the following separately:

- **Flights and cruise.** Check Aqua Nera's availability, connection times through Lima, flights to and from Easter Island, and transfers between northern and southern Chile.
- **Trains and private aviation.** Agree on the exact travel classes, boarding conditions, baggage restrictions, weather contingencies for helicopters and possible alternatives.
- **Guides and accommodation.** Russian-speaking assistance is provided on selected sections in Peru and Santiago. The guiding language on the remaining days should be specified in the personalised proposal.
- **Nature excursions.** Allow for weather restrictions and journey times in Torres del Paine, Puñihuil, river outings and lake excursions.

Altitude is another consideration. After the humid Amazonian lowlands, travellers reach Cusco, the Titicaca region, La Paz and the Bolivian Altiplano. Even when travelling in comfortable vehicles, **reduced atmospheric pressure remains a physiological challenge**. Anyone with heart or lung conditions should discuss the high-altitude stages with a doctor before travelling; reducing exertion during the first days at altitude can also help.

## When to plan the journey

There is no single month with ideal weather throughout this itinerary. The Amazon, central Andes, Atacama, Rapa Nui and Patagonia all have different seasonal patterns. For example, Uyuni's mirror-like surface depends on rainfall, while activities in Patagonia depend on wind and current weather. It is impossible to guarantee ideal conditions for every nature excursion in one travel period.

A sensible approach is to identify two or three must-have experiences and choose the dates around them, taking the cruise, trains and flights into account. If Machu Picchu and Uyuni are the priorities, compare this itinerary with shorter [Peru and Bolivia tours](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) or a [route through the southern Altiplano](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/). If the aim is to combine Rapa Nui, Chilean Patagonia and an Amazon cruise in one journey, the 33-day itinerary serves a different purpose.

## Frequently asked questions about the 33-day VIP itinerary

### How many countries are in the main programme?

**Three: Peru, Bolivia and Chile.** The journey begins in Lima and ends in Santiago.

### How long is the Aqua Nera cruise?

**Five days and four nights, from day 4 to day 8** of the complete itinerary. The exact river excursions follow the ship's programme.

### Is Easter Island part of the main itinerary?

**Yes.** Days 22–24 are dedicated to Rapa Nui, including Rano Kau, Orongo and sites with moai.

### Is there a confirmed price for the 33 days?

**There is no single published amount in the current tour listing.** Price, dates, currency and included services are determined in a personalised proposal.

### Will every excursion take place regardless of weather?

**No.** The Torres del Paine itinerary and visit to Puñihuil, in particular, depend on weather conditions; aviation and water-based excursions also require safe conditions.

## A 14-day grand tour of South America: preparing for three countries

The journey through Peru, Bolivia and Chile covers **14 days and 13 nights**. It begins in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), continues through Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), then takes in Lake Titicaca, [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and the high-altitude lagoons of the Bolivian Altiplano. After an overland border crossing into Chile, the journey continues through [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and finishes in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

This is a full itinerary with several significant changes in altitude and climate. Conditions differ between the Pacific coast, the high-altitude lake, the cold salt flat and Chile's major city. The main consideration before choosing the tour is therefore your readiness for frequent road journeys, domestic flights and several days at high elevation.

## The itinerary day by day

The first two days are devoted to Lima and its historic centre. Day 3 involves a flight to Cusco, while day 4 is reserved for Machu Picchu. The journey then moves into the Peruvian highlands: a coach transfer to Puno on day 5, followed on day 6 by a visit to [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and the Uros Islands.

Day 7 links Peru and Bolivia via Copacabana and leads to La Paz. After exploring the city, travellers move to Uyuni on day 9 to see the salt flat and Incahuasi Island. Day 10 includes the Siloli Desert, several high-altitude lagoons and an overnight stay around Ojo de Perdiz.

Day 11 is among the most unusual for scenery and travelling: [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), geothermal fields, Lake Chalviri, Laguna Verde and the border crossing into Chile. San Pedro de Atacama follows. Day 12 includes a transfer to Calama Airport and a flight to Santiago. Day 13 is dedicated to the Chilean capital, while day 14 covers the transfer for the international departure.

The result is a complete route through three countries in which the order of travel matters. The transitions themselves are part of the experience, especially the Uyuni–southern lagoons–Atacama section.

## Changes in altitude: why preparation matters

During the journey, travellers reach high-altitude areas of the Andes several times. Coastal Lima is followed by Cusco, then Titicaca and La Paz, and later the Altiplano and southern Bolivia's lagoons. Individual responses to altitude vary. Even without a challenging ascent in the programme, long vehicle journeys and walking in thin air can be tiring.

Travellers with cardiovascular, respiratory or other significant medical conditions should discuss the planned elevations with a doctor in advance. It is also helpful to recognise symptoms of altitude sickness and agree on a reasonable pace for the first few days. The description "vehicle-based excursion" does not mean there is no altitude-related strain.

Pack clothes that can be layered. Warm days in Lima and Santiago do not rule out cold nights, wind and intense sunlight at higher elevations. For Bolivia, warm outerwear, closed shoes, sun protection and a small supply of essentials in hand luggage are particularly useful.

## What makes each country distinctive

**Peru:** Lima's historic architecture, Inca heritage in Cusco and Machu Picchu, and the culture of the highlands around Titicaca. The main trade-off is the relatively rapid progression from the ocean coast to higher elevations.

**Bolivia:** [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) salt flat, the Siloli Desert and lagoons frequented by flamingos. This section offers the most striking contrasts in scenery, but also includes long drives across exposed plateaus.

**Chile:** crossing through the Atacama, time to rest after the high-altitude sections and a city visit in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). It is important to coordinate the overland route with the flight from Calama without allowing too short a connection.

Each stage serves a different purpose. If Machu Picchu is your only priority, the long sequence through Uyuni and Chile may be more than you need. You can also compare [Peru tours](/peru/tour/) and [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/). If the aim is to experience several Andean environments in one trip, the three-country combination offers much more variety than a single-country journey.

## Domestic flights and border crossings

The route includes flights from Lima to Cusco, La Paz to Uyuni and Calama to Santiago. **These domestic flights are explicitly listed among the services not included**, as is the international flight ticket. Flight times must be coordinated so that essential excursions are not shortened and there is some allowance for schedule changes.

The Peru–Bolivia and Bolivia–Chile borders are crossed overland. Visa and passport requirements depend on nationality, residence status and the countries' current rules. They should be checked against official sources for each traveller before dates are finally confirmed. Permission to enter one country cannot automatically be treated as permission to enter its neighbour.

Payments for additional services and the acceptance of bank cards also vary by country. In some high-altitude areas, relying exclusively on cashless payments is inadvisable. It is better to agree on likely expenses and a backup payment method in advance, without assuming that cards from any particular bank will be accepted.

## What the base price includes

The tour includes standard accommodation, specified meals, excursions and admission tickets, driver-operated transfers, a rail ticket on the Aguas Calientes–Cusco section and the tourist group coach from Cusco to Puno. Russian-speaking guides are specified for Lima, the Cusco city tour, La Paz and Santiago. English-speaking guides work on the remaining sections, while a Russian-speaking escort can be requested for an additional charge.

International flights, the listed domestic flights, airport charges, meals outside the programme, optional excursions and personal expenses are paid separately. We offer **six rate options for 2027**, depending on the number of participants and SGL/DBL/TPL accommodation. The tour price therefore needs to be compared with the group composition in mind, rather than simply the lowest amount shown in a headline.

## Easter Island: an extension, not part of the 14 days

**Easter Island is not included in the main 14-day journey.** It is a separate optional extension lasting **three days and two nights**. It covers Rapa Nui archaeological areas, the Rano Raraku volcano, the Ahu Tongariki platform, Orongo village and Anakena Beach.

The extension includes group excursions in English and accommodation in a 3-star hotel; a private format and Russian-speaking guide are available for an additional charge. It has its own accommodation-based price table, which must be added separately to the base tour. International and local flights need to be coordinated with the extended trip duration.

If Rapa Nui archaeology is your main dream, it makes more sense to book it as a substantial separate experience than to try to squeeze it into a free evening in Santiago. Flight times and actual schedules are essential here.

## Frequently asked questions about the Peru–Bolivia–Chile tour

### Is Machu Picchu included in the 14-day programme?

Yes. [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is scheduled for day 4, and the railway ticket for the return section towards Cusco is listed among included services.

### Is a trip to Easter Island compulsory?

No. The main programme ends in Santiago on day 14. Easter Island is offered separately as a three-day, two-night extension.

### Are all flights included in the price?

No. The international flight and domestic flights from Lima to Cusco, La Paz to Uyuni and Calama to Santiago are listed among excluded services.

### Is special physical training necessary?

The main programme does not include a sporting ascent, but it does involve long journeys and high-altitude areas. When assessing whether the route is suitable, consider your tolerance of altitude and any individual medical restrictions.

## Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama: what a 15-day journey through three countries offers

This 15-day itinerary connects [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), both sides of Iguazu Falls, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the Pacific coast and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The main reason to choose it is the gradual progression from major cities and cultural excursions to the radically different landscapes of northern Chile.

Unlike the New Year group itineraries, this programme includes **private excursions and transfers with a Russian-speaking guide**. More time is dedicated to Chile: in addition to Santiago, travellers visit [Valparaiso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) and spend two nights in San Pedro de Atacama. This makes it possible to visit not only Moon Valley but also lagoons, the salt flat and geysers.

## How the 14 nights are allocated

| Area | Nights and experiences |
| --- | --- |
| Rio de Janeiro | 3; Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain |
| Foz do Iguaçu | 2; both sides of the waterfalls |
| Buenos Aires | 3; tango, gauchos and the city |
| Santiago de Chile | 4; the capital and Pacific coast |
| San Pedro de Atacama | 2; desert and highlands |

Flights and overland transfers follow this sequence. When planning, remember that **international and domestic flights are not included in the base price**. This is one significant difference between the 15-day option and the two New Year itineraries.

## Brazil and Argentina: both sides of Iguazu and time in Buenos Aires

In Rio, the programme spreads its main high viewpoints across separate days: Sugarloaf Mountain on one day and Corcovado with the Christ the Redeemer statue on another. A flight to the waterfalls follows. On the Brazilian side, near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), visitors see the falls from viewpoints along the canyon. On the Argentine side, reached via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), walkways pass among the cascades, including towards Devil's Throat.

Both visits are part of the main itinerary. Macuco Safari and the Bird Park are offered separately as possible optional excursions, and their timing and cost should be considered before departure.

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the itinerary continues with a city tour, a tango evening and a full day at a gaucho ranch. The ranch programme describes horse riding, a traditional lunch, displays of horsemanship and lasso skills. This gives the Argentine section considerably more depth than a brief stop for a single city excursion.

## Chile: how the capital, ocean and Atacama differ

A city tour is planned in Santiago, with a separate day for [Valparaiso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). The road from the capital passes through Curacaví and Casablanca, a region known for wineries and white wines. The published itinerary describes Valparaiso's hills, viewpoints and port in detail, along with a walk in Viña del Mar. **Wine tasting at a winery is not listed among the included services**, so it should not be added to the offer without agreement.

The second part of Chile begins with a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). On the first day, travellers visit [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/), with its rock formations, dry depressions and long shadows at sunset. This landscape contrasts sharply with the coast.

The following day is devoted to the high-altitude Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons, a stop in Socaire and the [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/), including Chaxa Lagoon. Flamingos can be observed in this area, although the behaviour of wild birds and the weather cannot be guaranteed. Toconao is also mentioned in the itinerary.

## Sunrise at El Tatio: the earliest and coldest departure

The penultimate excursion day starts exceptionally early. The group travels to the [El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) to see columns of steam at sunrise. This geothermal field lies **above 4,300 metres** above sea level. Chile's official tourism portal notes that morning excursions require departure from San Pedro before dawn, when conditions are particularly cold.

Warm layers, a hat, gloves, sun protection and water are needed for this day. Altitude can affect wellbeing even without strenuous physical activity. Anyone with heart or lung conditions or other risk factors should discuss the journey with a doctor beforehand.

On the return route, the programme includes a stop at Machuca, followed by a transfer to Calama, a flight to Santiago and hotel accommodation. The next day is the departure home. El Tatio is therefore combined with quite an extensive chain of travel, which should be taken into account when buying separate flight tickets.

## Hotels, guides, tickets and extra expenses

The price includes **4-star hotels or equivalent with breakfast, private excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, private transfers with drivers and admission tickets**. Optional excursions, international and domestic flights, and meals and drinks during travel are paid for separately.

To calculate the final budget, account for flights between Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago and Calama as required by the programme. The range of included services differs from the [10-day New Year group tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-2027-10-days/), which includes the listed regional flights. ## Suriname, French Guiana and Guyana in seven days: how the itinerary works

[Suriname](/suriname/), [French Guiana](/french-guiana/) and [Guyana](/guyana/) lie beside one another on South America's Atlantic coast, yet differ considerably in language, history and administration. Dutch is the official language of Suriname, French of French Guiana and English of Guyana. French Guiana is an overseas region of France rather than an independent country.

Ada Tours' seven-day journey combines urban history, space exploration, colonial heritage and tropical nature. A distinctive feature is **two different ways of crossing borders**: by river between Suriname and French Guiana, and on a regional flight from Suriname to Guyana. The programme lasts **seven days and six nights**, beginning in Paramaribo and ending in Georgetown.

## Sequence of stops

| Days | Main part of the journey |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Paramaribo and a historic plantation |
| 3–4 | Transfer to French Guiana, Kourou and the islands |
| 5 | Cayenne, Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni and return to Suriname |
| 6 | Georgetown and a flight to Kaieteur Falls |
| 7 | Transfer to Georgetown airport |

This sequence involves returning to Suriname after the French Guiana section. When checking travel documents, it is important to account for both river border crossings rather than assuming that French Guiana is a visa-free one-day transit for all nationalities.

## Paramaribo: wooden architecture and plantation history

The first introduction to the region takes place in [Paramaribo](/suriname/place/paramaribo/). The city tour includes Independence Square, the Palm Garden, Fort Zeelandia and the waterfront. Paramaribo's historic centre is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site thanks to its preserved urban plan and distinctive combination of European and local building traditions.

After visiting a market selling local produce and spices, the route continues to the historic Peperpot plantation. This day reveals Suriname's past beyond the familiar image of a tropical coast. Travellers explore both city architecture and a place closely associated with the colonial economy.

## Crossing the border into French Guiana

On day 3, the group travels to Albina and crosses the Marowijne River by boat to Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni. The crossing is made in small boats, with border formalities on both sides. The journey then continues overland towards the [Guiana Space Centre at Kourou](/french-guiana/place/guiana-space-centre/).

The main practical point is that the crossing connects territories with different entry requirements. **Permission to enter one country or the Schengen Area must not automatically be treated as confirmation that a traveller can enter all three parts of the itinerary.** Requirements need to be checked separately for each nationality, direction of travel and travel date. We help coordinate the necessary checks and the order of transfers before the booking is finalised.

## Kourou space centre and islands of the former penal colony

The [Guiana Space Centre](/french-guiana/place/guiana-space-centre/) at Kourou is an operating launch site for European rockets. The excursion introduces visitors to its infrastructure. Safety requirements matter at an active spaceport: the official centre warns that visitor routes may change during launch preparations and that tours may be suspended on certain days. An included visit to the space centre therefore **does not mean a rocket launch is guaranteed**.

The next day involves a catamaran journey to islands associated with the history of the French penal system, including [Devil's Island](/french-guiana/place/devils-island/). The excursion focuses on imprisonment and life in an isolated island settlement. The sea crossing, disembarkation and time ashore depend on sea conditions and the arrangements for the particular excursion.

Day 5 continues this historical theme with [Cayenne](/french-guiana/place/cayenne/) and the former prison camp at Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni, after which the group returns to Paramaribo.

## Guyana and Kaieteur: the natural highlight

The final full sightseeing day begins in [Georgetown](/guyana/place/georgetown/), with a city tour, architectural sights and Stabroek Market. A separate flight then departs from Ogle Airport towards [Kaieteur National Park](/guyana/place/kaieteur-national-park/).

Kaieteur is far from the principal urban roads, making the flight an important part of the logistics. The programme includes a flight to the falls and approximately two hours on site, with visits to viewpoints. The return flight brings travellers back to Georgetown. Encounters with birds and other wildlife are possible, but cannot be guaranteed.

Weather and flying conditions are especially important on this day. When arranging international flights after the tour, it is sensible to allow sufficient time in case the small-aircraft schedule changes.

## What's included and what's paid separately

The tour price includes **3-star hotels with breakfast**, ground transfers in air-conditioned minivans, an English-speaking guide throughout the programme, specified meals, admission tickets and taxes. It also explicitly includes **the Suriname–Guyana flight, the flight to Kaieteur, the overland transfer and the river crossing into French Guiana**.

Visas, flights to the starting point and onward from the finish, and meals beyond those specified are additional expenses. An important detail when booking flights is that **day 7 ends in Georgetown**, so the final airport and departure arrangements should be checked against the confirmed programme.

## Who the three-Guianas journey suits

This itinerary will appeal to travellers interested in **parts of northeastern South America rarely combined in one journey**. Languages, cities, border arrangements and even the subject of the excursions change during the week: from wooden architecture and a space centre to a tropical waterfall.

If a long nature trek is your main priority rather than an overview of three territories, a different pace may be preferable. This programme focuses on sightseeing, with several significant transport sections. Other nearby destinations are featured in our [multi-country travel catalogue](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about the three Guianas

### Is French Guiana a separate country?

No. It is an overseas territory of France with its own entry requirements, which must be checked for each traveller's nationality and specific route.

### How do travellers reach Kaieteur Falls?

By plane from Georgetown via Ogle Airport. The flight and the excursion to the waterfall are listed among the included services.

### Can visitors watch a rocket launch at Kourou?

A scheduled tour of the space centre does not guarantee a launch. Access to particular buildings and areas depends on the spaceport's operational schedule.

### What language are the excursions conducted in?

The included services specify an **English-speaking guide** throughout the programme. Russian-speaking accompaniment is not listed as an included service.
